published.citation: Shporer et al. 2014, the temperature of a black body showing the same occultation depths in all four bands: 2750 +/- 160 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...788...92S/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse in the Kepler, Ks, 3.6 µm and 4.5 µm bands together (Kepler, Palomar WIRC and Spitzer IRAC) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: the paper's own value; Esteves et al. 2015's Kepler-band 3,490 K assumes no reflected light and is not used
temperature.band: the Kepler, Ks, 3.6 µm and 4.5 µm bands together
temperature.facility: Kepler, Palomar WIRC and Spitzer IRAC
